name: Adani Energy Solutions Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest private transmission company (29,802 ckm, 1.43 lakh MVA, 16 states; Q2 FY27 transmission EBITDA margin 92%), plus Mumbai distribution (AEML, ~13 mn consumers incl. MUL; RAB Rs 10,456 cr), a smart-metering platform (14.8 mn installed, 24.6 mn order book, Rs 29,519 cr) and a fast-growing Energy Solutions trading/RTC platform (Q2 operating EBITDA Rs 803 cr). Q2 FY27 total income Rs 10,239 cr (+51%), EBITDA Rs 3,548 cr (+67%), PAT Rs 1,364 cr (+145%). Transmission under construction ~Rs 87,000 cr (15 projects); FY27 transmission capex ~Rs 14,000 cr. Promoters 73.4%; stock Rs 1,453 (+47% in 12m, -10% in 3m); P/E 48; borrowings Rs 51.8k cr.

revenue_mix.segment: Energy Solutions platform (power trading, RTC supply, C&I)
revenue_mix.geography: India (H1 FY27 operating revenue Rs 4,103 cr of Rs 14,351 cr)

exposures.mechanism: Long-duration regulated/TBCB annuity compounder: P/E 48, EV ~Rs 2.3 lakh cr vs mcap Rs 1.77 lakh cr (EV/MCap ~1.3; net debt ~Rs 49k cr on Rs 51.8k cr borrowings, screener Sep-26). +25bp on a ~9% WACC with equity duration ~20 => ~-5%, but ~60% of cash flows are CERC-fixed 25-35 yr tariffs whose RoE does not reset with yields, so only ~40% of the duration effect is realised => -2.0. Pack shows no significant empirical beta to US 10y (-1.02, t -0.9).

evidence.note: Mcap Rs 1,77,475 cr, P/E 47.9, borrowings Rs 51,801 cr (Sep-26)
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Funding-cost channel only (discount-rate channel is carried by F_GSEC_10Y_IN). Mgmt (23 Oct call): 'a significant portion of our debt is fixed rate or hedged', no material rate volatility expected in P&L. Illustrative: Rs 51.8k cr debt x ~35% floating x 25bp = Rs 45 cr/yr vs TTM PBT ~Rs 4.9k cr = -0.9% PAT; AEML RAB interest is partly allowed in tariff; x EV/MCap 1.3 x persistence 1.0 => ~-1.2.

evidence.note: Kandarp Patel: significant portion of debt fixed/hedged; no volatility expected from FX or rates
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Rs 87,000 cr transmission order book + 14,000 cr FY27 transmission capex + smart-meter capex must be refinanced/raised at project level; group spreads widen first in stress. +50bp on ~Rs 25k cr refinanced over 2 yrs = Rs 125 cr/yr = ~-2.5% of TTM PBT; capitalised at ~10x on 1.3 EV/MCap with persistence 0.5 and offset by regulated pass-through => -2.2. Raised Rs 3,500 cr QIP in H1 FY27 which lowers near-term need.

evidence.note: Raised Rs 3,500 cr via QIP; transmission under-construction pipeline ~Rs 87,000 cr
Transmission capex guidance ~Rs 14,000 cr FY27; Rs 8-9k cr in H2

exposures.mechanism: Transmission is the bottleneck for renewables (Khavda curtailment); stronger support (PM-DHARA Rs 1.86 lakh cr corridor scheme approved 30 Sep 2026; near-term tender pipeline ~Rs 1.4 lakh cr) lifts AESL's addressable awards. Order book Rs 87k cr; each +Rs 10k cr of wins at ~15% equity IRR spread adds ~Rs 1.5k cr NPV-at-risk ~ +0.8% of mcap; policy step expected to add ~Rs 30-40k cr of awards over 2 yrs to AESL's ~25-30% bid share => ~+4. Stock +5.5% on 1 Oct, 3rd straight up day (coincident, not proven causal).

evidence.note: Cabinet approved Rs 1.86 lakh crore PM-DHARA green energy transmission scheme on 30 Sep 2026 (DD India, ThePrint, Moneycontrol headlines)

evidence.source: https://www.business-standard.com (via Google News RSS: 'Adani Energy Solutions gains 5.5%; extends winning streak to 3rd session')
evidence.note: Stock +5.5% on 1 Oct 2026 after PM-DHARA approval (headline)
Near-term transmission tendering pipeline ~Rs 1.4 lakh crore

exposures.mechanism: Grid and electrification capex theme underpins the Rs 1.4 lakh cr near-term tender pipeline, HVDC awards and 86 mn-meter national smart-meter opportunity (AESL order book 24.6 mn meters, Rs 29,519 cr). +1 SSU assumed to add ~Rs 40k cr awards (+2.5% of EV/year growth) over 2 years; at EV/MCap 1.3 and persistence 1.0 => ~+5, wide range because award timing is lumpy.

evidence.note: Smart-meter order book 24.6 mn meters, Rs 29,519 cr; national opportunity 86 mn meters
Fortune India: order book rises to Rs 87,000 cr

exposures.mechanism: Mumbai distribution units +11% YoY (2,930 vs 2,650 MU), MUL +26%; distribution EBITDA is regulated (RAB Rs 10,456 cr) so only 40% of volume gain converts, but the Energy Solutions platform (Q2 operating EBITDA Rs 803 cr of Rs 3,070 cr = 26%) earns on trading/RTC volumes (12.2 bn units Q2). +3pp demand ~ +3% energy-solutions volume => ~+1.5% EBITDA x 1.3 x 0.8 persistence => ~+1.5.

evidence.note: AEML units sold +11%; Energy Solutions Q2 operating EBITDA Rs 803 cr
Q2 energy-solutions sales 12.2 bn units

exposures.mechanism: Energy Solutions earns a spread between sourced supply (solar/wind 4.6 GW, ~3.5 GWh BESS tie-ups) and customer tariffs; legacy merchant volumes benefit from high spot prices but newly signed fixed-price RTC to MSEDCL (2,500 MW, 25 yrs) means rising spot prices raise sourcing risk until capacity is tied up (mgmt cites 'timing mismatches'). Net direction ambiguous; spot +15% x merchant volume ~9.5 bn units tilt gives about +1% EBITDA offset by mismatch => ~+0.4.

evidence.note: Q&A: merchant volumes being converted to long-term PPAs; margin timing mismatches while capacity tied up
2,500 MW RTC PPA with MSEDCL for 25 years

exposures.mechanism: Transmission towers, conductors and substation steel are ~35% of project cost; TBCB tariffs are fixed at award, so cost inflation falls on the developer. +7% steel => +2.5% on the ~Rs 25k cr of un-contracted capex in 2 yrs = Rs 600 cr x 50% unrecoverable = Rs 300 cr = -0.17% of mcap; plus order-book re-pricing risk on bids => ~-0.8. Pack empirical F_STEEL_GLOBAL is +3.42 (t +2.2) with market beta 1.62: sign conflicts, likely risk-on co-movement rather than fundamentals; weight deliberately kept negative.

evidence.note: All contracts awarded for H2 capex, but ROW and execution delays in Gujarat
Pack empirical: F_STEEL_GLOBAL +3.42 per SSU, t +2.2

exposures.mechanism: Imported HVDC/substation equipment and some USD bonds (model knowledge: AESL has USD senior notes) vs mostly INR revenues. Mgmt says debt largely fixed/hedged so no P&L volatility. +3% USDINR on ~15% unhedged USD exposure of Rs 49k cr net debt = Rs 220 cr = -0.12% mcap; capex import content adds ~-0.3%; EV/MCap 1.3 => ~-1.0 with low confidence. Rupee is at 94.5 (+6.5% in 12m).

evidence.note: Debt largely fixed rate or hedged; no FX volatility expected in P&L
Borrowings Rs 51,801 cr

exposures.mechanism: Distribution reform / privatisation and parallel-licence opportunities (AESL seeks 'expansion of distribution network through parallel licenses'); smart-meter rollout is tied to state discoms' payment security. +1 SSU (reform progress) lifts probability and size of new distribution licences and de-risks Rs 29.5k cr smart-meter receivables: assumed +Rs 5k cr NPV (2.8% of mcap) at 60% realisation => ~+3.

evidence.note: Expansion of distribution via parallel licences; smart meters under implementation 24.6 mn
Smart-meter slow Q2 due to discom meter-type changes (call)

exposures.mechanism: Energy Solutions targets C&I, data centres and utilities (supply tie-up ~4.6 GW RE + 3.5 GWh BESS); Mumbai/Navi Mumbai data-centre load raises AEML volumes and grid investment. +1 SSU => +10% C&I volume growth assumption; Energy Solutions EBITDA run-rate Rs 3.2k cr/yr x 10% x 1.3 x 0.6 => +1.8.

evidence.note: Energy Solutions platform catering to C&I, data centers and utilities
Mgmt on consumer-side tie-ups starting last quarter of this year

exposures.mechanism: High-beta (market beta 1.6) Adani-group stock whose FII holding has fallen 17.6% (Mar-25) -> 9.6% (Sep-26) while DIIs rose 6.3% -> 13.6% and promoter 73.4% (Sep-26); free float ~26%. +US$5bn FPI quarterly inflow ~ +2% Nifty (assumed) x beta 1.6 => +3.2; shrunk for the group-specific overhang => +2.8.

evidence.note: Shareholding: FIIs 9.57%, DIIs 13.61%, promoters 73.39% (Sep-26)

exposures.mechanism: No coal cost in transmission/distribution, but Energy Solutions trades power and AEML buys thermal power; higher imported coal lifts spot/merchant prices and trading margin on un-contracted volumes. Pack empirical +5.68 per SSU (t +1.9, beta 1.68) is much larger than any fundamental channel (+15% coal => spot +5-8% => ~+0.8% EBITDA => ~+0.5); the gap likely reflects shared risk-on/commodity-cycle factor, flagged for the assembler to shrink.

evidence.note: Pack empirical: F_COAL_INTL +5.68 per SSU, t +1.9
Over half of coal plants at critically low stocks; captive plants ordered to maximise output from 1 Oct (Times of India 21 Oct, Reuters 28 Sep 2026 headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Escalation raises oil/LNG, inflation and yields (RBI turned hawkish 7 Oct), hitting high-multiple utilities; offset by energy-security push that accelerates grid and domestic-supply capex. AESL has no direct Gulf cash flow. Net -0.6 per +1 SSU, low confidence.
